A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EasyHOI and contain complete main papers and six-page supplementary materials. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on Arctic, OakInk, and DexYCB, quantitative ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative experiments in the supplementary material.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, and supplementary qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same segmentation, inpainting, hand/object reconstruction components and three-stage camera setup, contact alignment, and hand refinement procedure. The supplementary implementation of these components is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate single-image hand-object reconstruction on Arctic, OakInk, DexYCB, and collected in-the-wild images. The supplementary examples represent the same datasets and scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains IHOI, AlignSDF, gSDF, and MOHO, with AlignSDF and gSDF excluded from DexYCB in both versions. Qualitative comparisons retain IHOI/MOHO and the InstantMesh-versus-Tripo3D comparison. Newly cited video methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Both specify 500 randomly selected, force-closure-filtered images per dataset, the same zero-shot exclusions, and HaMeR hand estimates for baselines. Metrics, 5/10 mm F-score thresholds, optimization settings, and 1,000-step simulation evaluation are unchanged.

E4.justification: The optimization-stage ablations in Table 2/Figure 5 and loss ablations in Table 3/Figure 7 are unchanged. Supplementary segmentation examples, the inpainting comparison in Figure 10, and reconstruction-model comparison in Figure 15 are also retained.

E5.justification: Tables 2–3 retain identical mean and standard-deviation reporting. Neither version provides additional repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 contain the same numerical entries. For example, EasyHOI's Table 1 Chamfer distances remain 1.089, 1.035, and 1.628 on Arctic, OakInk, and DexYCB. Qualitative reconstructions and reported findings also match, including the appendices.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, Wasserstein and optimal-transport expressions, losses in Equations 1–8, and supplementary contact-mask definitions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: combining large-model priors with optimization for physically plausible single-image reconstruction, generalization to unseen scenes, and superiority over the evaluated baselines.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations of contact alignment, loss-ablation effects, and extensibility to stronger reconstruction models. The conclusion's limitation concerning failures of the underlying large models remains unchanged, although it moves onto PDF page 9 in v3.

D1.justification: The A40 hardware, learning rates, stopping criteria, registration iterations, and loss weights are unchanged. Both appendices already provide the same prompts, segmentation and mesh-processing details, and four-depth-layer implementation. Project access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds four video-based reconstruction references: HOLD, Hasson's photometric-consistency work, Huang's monocular-video reconstruction, and Ye's diffusion-guided interaction clips. It replaces the brief feature-fusion/geometry/physics grouping with an input-based distinction and adds existing AlignSDF, gSDF, and MOHO citations to the implicit-shape discussion.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 2.1, with a few small wording edits elsewhere. v3 expands affiliations, adds corresponding-author and visit information, and introduces acknowledgements. Supplementary Sections 6–8 become Sections 7–9; the scientific narrative otherwise remains stable.

P2.justification: Expanded front matter shifts Figure 1 and moves the introduction to page 2; subsequent text and references reflow. Figures 1–15 and Tables 1–3 retain their contents and designs, and the final three supplementary pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves scholarly context by covering video-based reconstruction and connecting existing single-view baselines to Section 2.1. The revised input-based grouping compresses the earlier mechanism-based taxonomy but better contextualizes the single-image task. Methods, experimental support, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited.
